FRENCH — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

2. When practising Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.

3. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

4. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.

5. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Thank you
   D. Excuse me

6. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.

7. When practising Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information Attention Note taking Vocabulary.

8. When practising Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

9. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. porte
   B. chaise
   C. livre
   D. fenêtre

10. When practising Interactive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing Clarity Punctuation Grammar and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing Orthography Vocabulary Letter formation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing Clarity Fluidity Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
